chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

A time will come over people when only the defamer will be brought near, only the vicious will be regarded as witty, and only the just will be regarded as weak. They will consider charity a burden, kinship ties an obligation, and worship a means of claiming greatness over people. At that time, authority will be through the counsel of women, the posting of young boys, and the administration by eunuchs.

key_terms.الْمَاحِلُ: The defamer or one who speaks ill of others to gain favor
key_terms.صِلَةَ الرَّحِمِ: Kinship ties or maintaining family relations

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of moral decline and weak governance according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) describes a period of moral and social decline where superficial traits replace true virtue, leading to a specific type of governance characterized by the influence of women, children, and eunuchs, reflecting a departure from just leadership. This narration, often cited in discussions of the 'Era of Neglect' (Zaman al-Gha'bah), highlights how societal inversion—where the righteous are undervalued and the wicked elevated—precipitates political instability and the rise of weak or incompetent rulers. The mention of 'women, children, and eunuchs' symbolizes a lack of mature, decisive authority, a theme deeply resonant in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the decline of the Umayyad and early Abbasid periods.
